reviews.summary: The patch adds the requested dot guard in Blueprint.__init__ (src/flask/blueprints.py:197-198), raises ValueError with the expected message before self.name assignment, and updates the docstring, docs/blueprints.rst, and CHANGES.rst under Version 2.0.1 Unreleased. Dotted names are rejected at construction (B1) while dot-free names still construct and keep their names (B2); the guard does not touch nested-registration or add_url_rule dot assertions. Protected tests/config are unmodified. compileall and flake8 pass on the changed source. The only new suite failure is a stale protected test that constructs a dotted blueprint name, which is directly authorized by the request to reject dots; nested-runtime checks are blocked by an unrelated Werkzeug 2.3.7 environment incompatibility, but code inspection shows dot-free/nested paths are unaffected.

reviews.summary: The patch adds a pre-artist 1D validation in Axes3D.plot and makes art3d.line_2d_to_3d atomic, so a 2D-coordinate 3D line plot raises a descriptive ValueError before any Line3D is created, and any conversion failure restores Line2D. Code reading confirms no previously working input shape is rejected: every ndim>1 case already failed in Line3D.set_3d_properties via np.broadcast_to (before/inside the conversion), so only the resulting half-converted artist state changes. Existing mplot3d tests and the configured visible syntax check pass, and the scratch receipt shows the reported trigger followed by a clean draw.

The patch replaces the discarded chararray.replace() call with an in-place assignment (`output_field[:] = output_field.replace(...)`), which is exactly the requested D-exponent fix. Historical receipts show explicit D and default/derived D25.17 ASCII columns now write D exponents with field widths preserved, E/F/A/I columns are unchanged, and the changed-value write/read script finished with ALL CHECKS PASSED. test_table.py passed 84 tests with 2 skips. The two test_core.py failures are shown by the baseline stash receipt to fail identically with the fix reverted, so they are pre-existing environment/mock failures, not regressions. The supplied patch touches only astropy/io/fits/fitsrec.py.

The one-line patch forwards permute into the recursive diophantine call used when syms differs from the alphabetically sorted variable order, so the issue repro with syms=(n,m), permute=True now produces the full signed-permutation solution set before tuple reordering. The change only broadens results for the explicitly requested permute=True case, leaves default/permute=False and syms ordering behavior intact, and touches only the affected public entry point. Existing module tests and the visible syntax check passed.

reviews.summary: The patch removes the reported corruption: Axes3D.plot validates before creating artists, and line_2d_to_3d restores Line2D on conversion failure, so no Line3D lacking _verts3d can persist (confirmed by the /tmp/check_issue.py receipt and by the 136 passing test_mplot3d tests plus the syntax check). However, the blanket np.ndim > 1 guard is broader than the reported trigger and rejects shapes the pre-change code handled correctly (2D y that Axes.plot splits into per-column datasets, e.g. column vectors and multi-line plots), so it is an unauthorized compatibility narrowing.
findings: lib/mpl_toolkits/mplot3d/axes3d.py:1279-1289 — the new guard `any(np.ndim(data) > 1 for data in (xs, ys, zs))` rejects every non-1D coordinate, including shapes the previous implementation accepted. Trigger: `ax = plt.figure().add_subplot(projection='3d'); ax.plot(np.arange(3), np.arange(3)[:, None], 0)` (or `ax.plot(np.arange(3), np.arange(6).reshape(3, 2), np.arange(3))`). Pre-change behavior: Axes.plot/_plot_args treats 2D y as one dataset per column (x of length M, zs broadcast to `np.shape(xs)` = (M,)) and each resulting 1D Line2D converts successfully, producing valid Line3D artists that draw. Post-change behavior: ValueError before any artist is created. Expected: the corruption fix must not reject these previously working call paths; validate only the shape that actually cannot be converted (e.g. per-line zs/len(xs) compatibility) or rely on the atomic conversion in art3d.line_2d_to_3d, which already prevents the reported half-converted Line3D. Neither an existing test asserting rejection of this shape nor an explicit statement in the original request authorizes it; the docstring/model-authored ledger is not such authority.

reviews.summary: The patch makes the D-exponent replacement effective with the minimal in-place assignment in FITS_rec._scale_back_ascii (astropy/io/fits/fitsrec.py:1264-1266), matching the safe-default approach in the plan. A verification script receipt shows explicit D25.17 and default float64 ASCII columns written with 'D+'/'D-' exponents while E, F, A, I raw output is unchanged, and the table test module passes (84 passed, 2 skipped) once the broken PYTEST_ADDOPTS env value is cleared; the two test_core failures are shown to fail identically with the fix stashed. The remaining precision-0 float read-back limitation is pre-existing formatting behavior (trailing decimal point) that the patch does not touch and that lies outside the original request.

The one-line patch propagates permute into the recursive call made in the syms-reordering branch of diophantine(). For the reported equation both syms=(m,n) and syms=(n,m) now return the complete 8-element set (the set is symmetric under entry swap, so the reordered tuples still equal the expected set), while permute=False base-solution behavior and syms ordering are unchanged. Paired native receipts show B1/B2/B3 failing before and passing after, and the full diophantine test module passes.

reviews.summary: The new early 1D validation plus atomic class revert fixes the reported corruption (A1/A2 receipts confirm the ValueError at plot time, empty ax.lines after the failed call, and a clean subsequent 1D draw; the full test_mplot3d.py run passes and the visible syntax check exits 0). However, the blanket `np.ndim(...) > 1` guard on xs/ys/zs also rejects an input shape the pre-change implementation accepted: 1D xs with a 2D (n, m) ys, which matplotlib's base `Axes.plot` intentionally expands into m lines (one per column). In the old Axes3D.plot, zs is broadcast to `np.shape(xs)` = (n,), each generated column has length n, so `Line3D.set_3d_properties` succeeds and the plot draws; with this patch it raises ValueError. The original request never asks to reject that shape, and no existing test asserts the rejection, so this is a compatibility narrowing that should be avoided (e.g. reject only the shapes that already failed pre-change, such as 2D xs/2D zs).
findings: lib/mpl_toolkits/mplot3d/axes3d.py (new guard in Axes3D.plot, ~line 1280): `if any(np.ndim(data) > 1 for data in (xs, ys, zs)): raise ValueError(...)` rejects 1D xs together with a 2D ys, e.g. `ax = plt.figure().add_subplot(projection='3d'); ax.plot(np.arange(3), np.array([[0., 1.], [1., 2.], [2., 3.]])); fig.canvas.draw()`. Expected: keep the previous behavior, where zs is broadcast to np.shape(xs)=(3,), base Axes.plot splits the 2D y into its two columns (ncx=1, ncy=2 -> two Line2D of length 3) and line_2d_to_3d succeeds for each (no _verts3d error, draw works). Observed: the new check raises ValueError('3D line plots require 1D ...') before any artist is created, so a documented base-plot input shape (2D y columns) that previously produced two 3D lines is now rejected; the original user request contains no authorization to reject this shape and no existing test asserts such rejection. The corruption fix should be preserved (e.g. atomic conversion/cleanup of only the failing artists) without narrowing this previously working input shape.
